# Imports and modules: `web/`

## Named exports, named imports

Export components, hooks, and helpers by name. A named export keeps one identifier at every
call site (renaming is a rename, not a silent alias), gives editors a reliable
go-to-definition, and lets a bundler drop what nobody imported. `web/src` already does this
throughout; a `export default` in a new file is a divergence, not a style choice.

Import them the same way. No namespace imports (`import * as helpers`), which defeat
tree-shaking and turn every call site into an indirection through an object. A third-party SDK
whose own documentation is namespace-shaped is the only exception, and there is none in this
tree today.

## No barrel files

Do not add an `index.ts` whose job is re-exporting its siblings. A barrel makes the bundler
pull in unrelated modules, fills the editor with tabs called `index.ts`, hides the real
location in a stack trace, and is the usual way a circular import gets introduced. Import the
file itself: `import { DataTable } from "@/shared/components/DataTable"`.

Two `index` files in the tree are the framework's spelling rather than ours, and both stay:

- `src/routeTree.gen.ts` is generated by the TanStack Router plugin. Never hand-edited.
- `src/routes/index.tsx` is how file-based routing spells the index route of a directory. The
  filename encodes a URL; it re-exports nothing.

`src/client/index.ts` is the third, and it is a deliberate exception with a job: it is the
alias layer over the generated `schema.ts` (`User` for `UserResponse`, the query-parameter
enums, the runtime guards). Import client types from `@/client`, never from `./schema`
directly, so the day the generator renames something there is one file to fix.

## Path aliases

`@/` resolves to `web/src` (`vite.config.ts` and `tsconfig.json`). Use it for anything outside
the current directory rather than climbing with `../../`. A relative `./Sibling` for a
tightly-coupled file in the same directory is clearer than the alias, and is fine.

**An overlay seam module is the exception, and it is not a style call.** The modules listed in
`src/overlaySeams.test.ts` (`app/nav/overlaySections.ts`, `overlayLabelOverrides.ts`,
`overlayWalletSlot.tsx`) each ship an inert default that a superset build replaces by aliasing
its `@/…` specifier. A relative import of one resolves to a path that alias never sees, so the
overlay's contribution vanishes with no error and the build renders the empty default it was
going to render anyway. Reach a seam by `@/…` even from the same directory; that test fails on a
relative one, and on a seam nothing imports. See [web/AGENTS.md](../../../web/AGENTS.md).

## The layer boundary is a lint error, not a review note

`web/biome.jsonc` enforces three rules, each with the alias form and the relative form spelled
out so `../../app/Sidebar` cannot dodge what `@/app/Sidebar` catches:

| Files | May not import | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/features/**` | `src/app/**` | A feature must not reach into the composition root. Lift the shared piece into `src/shared`, or let the shell pass it as a prop. |
| `src/shared/**` | `src/app/**`, `src/features/**` | `shared` is the leaf layer; dependencies point inward. |
| everything under `src/` | `overlay/**`, `@overlay/**` | An overlay tree exists only in the superset build composed in otari-ai. An import of it does not resolve in this repo's build. |

Feature-to-feature is deliberately allowed: keys pick models, budgets pick users.
`src/tests/` is deliberately outside the boundary, because a harness has to mount what the app
mounts, and it is the only place that may import `src/app`.

`src/architecture.test.ts` plants a violating import for each rule and asserts Biome rejects
it, so the rules cannot quietly stop being rules. It also asserts the layer set itself is
closed: a new directory directly under `src/` fails the test until a rule covers it.

## Test mocking

Mock modules by their specifier and keep the rest of the module real:

```ts
vi.mock("@/shared/helpers/clipboard", async () => {
  const actual = await vi.importActual<typeof import("@/shared/helpers/clipboard")>(
    "@/shared/helpers/clipboard",
  )
  return { ...actual, copyToClipboard: vi.fn() }
})
```

Wrap a hook-like export in `vi.fn()` when you replace one, so it behaves as a function
identity that lint and the React tooling can follow:

```ts
vi.mock("@tanstack/react-router", () => ({ useNavigate: vi.fn(() => navigate) }))
```

For the dashboard's own data, mock the transport rather than a module: the page tests spy on
`apiFetch` (`vi.spyOn(apiClient, "apiFetch")`) and let the real hooks, query keys, and
formatters run. See [testing.md](./testing.md).
